# POC scenario build

Execute the approved tasks of one scenario and stop only when every acceptance criterion is shown on screen in the demo walkthrough and passes its end-to-end test, on screens that look finished.

A POC is judged on screen. Speed of delivery and visual quality come first; code quality comes after. Take the shortest path that works and looks right.

## Hard constraints

1. Implement only the tasks of the approved `tasks.md`. A missing task is added in `tasks.md` with the reason, and approved by the user, before it is coded.
2. Write no unit or integration tests, and delete the test files the stack generators create (`.spec.ts` of components, JUnit classes). The only automated tests are the Playwright end-to-end tests of the demonstration tasks: one per acceptance criterion, written once the screens are stable. Never leave the build red between two tasks.
3. Never edit the specification, `spec.md`, `plan.md` or the constitution. Record any deviation in "Open points" of `<root>/state.md`, as a decision in `<root>/state/decisions.md` once the user settles it (with `Report to specification: yes` when it changes the described behaviour), and in one line on the task concerned in `tasks.md`.
4. Never guess. When a task is ambiguous, an element is missing (data, asset, access, interface contract, label) or the code would deviate from the plan, ask the user before coding it, following the rule on questions and approvals.
5. Task status is live, the team follows the build from it. Change the status of one task at a time, at the moment it changes: in progress before the first line of code of the task, done right after its build passes. Never work on two tasks at once, never mark several tasks in one change, and never mark a task done that was not in progress first. A task found already implemented (for example by an earlier scenario) still goes through in progress, then done with a note. In the Vibe Studio desktop application, these rules are enforced: code written without a task in progress and a second task in progress are refused.

## Procedure

1. Anchor. Read `poc.yml`, `<root>/build/constitution.md`, the "Framing" section of `state.md`, `state/decisions.md`, then `spec.md`, `plan.md` and `tasks.md` of the scenario. If the `Plan status:` line of `tasks.md` (or the legacy `Statut du plan`) does not say approved, stop and suggest the `poc-4-plan-scenario` skill. Run the `mark` command of the `poc-track-costs` skill with `--phase 5-build-scenario --scenario <n>`.
2. Pre-flight. Read every task and list for yourself what is unclear or missing to execute it. Ask the user each item, one question per call. Then ask how often to stop for review: after each group of tasks (recommended), only at the first screen and at the end, or only when blocked. Record the answer in `state/decisions.md`.
3. Environment. Check that the build and run commands of the constitution work. On the first scenario, create the project with the stack's own generator (CLI or MCP server of the stack) with unit test generation turned off, before writing code by hand. Set up the component library and theme of the constitution's visual identity at once. Check the generated versions against the constitution and fix any version that does not resolve; record the fix as a deviation. Ask before installing anything outside the project folder. Keep the `run` section of `poc.yml` in step with the constitution: when a service or a tool is added (database server, mail catcher, stub), add it in start order, show the change to the user and say that Vibe Studio will ask to confirm the commands again. When `run` is empty, propose it as `poc-4-plan-scenario` describes.
4. Task loop. Task status lives in `tasks.md`: `[ ]` to do, `[~]` in progress, `[x]` done, `[!]` blocked. Keep it exact, the team follows the build from it. For each task marked `[ ]` or `[~]`, in order:
   1. read the task and the ids it serves; if it raises a doubt, ask before coding;
   2. mark it in progress, before any code. When the launch context gives a Vibe Studio run id, call `vibe_studio_report` with `status: started` and `task: {id, status: in_progress}`: Vibe Studio writes `[~]` in `tasks.md` itself, so do not edit the marker. Otherwise, when the tool cannot be found or called, or when the result says the marker was not written, set it to `[~]` yourself;
   3. implement the fastest code that works, following the stack rules and the visual identity; reuse library components rather than building your own;
   4. run the build with the command of the constitution;
   5. when the task changes a screen, open it in the browser (Playwright MCP server) with the seed data, take a screenshot and fix what looks unfinished before moving on;
   6. mark it done the same way (report `task: {id, status: done}`, or set `[x]` yourself), then add a one-line note after `—` (what was done, screen shown);
   7. after three failed attempts on the same task, mark it blocked the same way (report `task: {id, status: blocked}`, or set `[!]` yourself) with the reason after `—`, record the blocker in "Open points" of `state.md` and ask the user how to proceed.
   Only one task is `[~]` at a time. A task left `[~]` by an interrupted session is resumed first.
   Before adding a dependency the plan does not name, read its license (`npm view <package> license`, the `<licenses>` of its Maven POM, or the registry page of the stack) and compare it with `compliance` of `poc.yml` and the policy of the `poc-7-check-compliance` skill, then ask the user to approve the dependency, with its license and its reason. A denied license stops the task: record it and ask the user for another option. A license to review is recorded on the task.
5. Review points. Stop at the frequency chosen in step 2, and always at the first screen of the first scenario. Show the screenshots of the screens built since the last stop, give the command or address to open the application, and ask: continue (recommended), adjust (the user says what), or stop. Turn each adjustment into a task in `tasks.md`, marked "user feedback", and run it through the task loop.
6. Visual finish. Review every screen of the scenario at the screen sizes of the constitution. Fix: alignment and spacing, components that do not match the theme, raw identifiers or technical codes shown to the user, unformatted dates and numbers, text overflow, empty, loading and error states, labels not in the output language. The screen must look like a product, not a prototype. When a label, a wording or a format is not settled by the specification, ask the user.
7. Demo walkthrough and end-to-end tests. When `stack.e2e` is `playwright`, write one test per acceptance criterion under `<paths.code>/e2e`, named after its id (for example `ac1-publish.spec.ts`). Each test starts from a clean start with the seed data, plays its step of the walkthrough of `plan.md` as the presenter would, checks the visible element that proves the criterion with user-facing locators (role, label, text), and saves a screenshot to `<root>/build/scenario-<n>/evidence/<id>.png`. Keep tests short: no page objects, no mocks of the application, no unit-level checks. Run them with the end-to-end command of the constitution; the screenshots must show the proving element, and two criteria may share a screen only if that element is visible on it. When `stack.e2e` is `none`, play the walkthrough with the Playwright MCP server and save the screenshots by hand. Fill the "Convergence" table of `tasks.md`: criterion, walkthrough step, status, screenshot, end-to-end test. A failing test is a criterion not shown: add a task marked "convergence" and go back to step 4. Fix the application, not the assertion, unless the test does not match the walkthrough. Stop after three convergence rounds and ask the user what to do with what remains.
8. Hand-over. Check that the services of `run` start from a clean start in their order and answer on their port. Show the user the screenshots of the walkthrough, how to start the application (the "Launch the POC" button of Vibe Studio, or the commands of `run`) and the command that replays the end-to-end tests before the demonstration. Ask whether to adjust something before the review (the user says what) or to move to the review (recommended). Adjustments go through the task loop and the walkthrough again.
9. Version control. If the project is a git repository, propose one commit per group of tasks with a message in the output language that names the scenario. Commit only after the user agrees. Open a pull request through the code host MCP server only if the user asks.
10. Record, following the rule on working files: a block "Phase 5: build of scenario <n>" in `state/journal.md` (date, tasks done, criteria shown in the walkthrough, convergence rounds, user feedback taken into account, deviations) and the row of "Progress".

## Review corrections

When `tasks.md` has tasks marked `[ ]` or `[~]` in "Review corrections" (French "Corrections issues de la revue"), run the pre-flight and the task loop on them only. A task marked "user feedback" comes from the user, through Vibe Studio or the chat, without a review: in the pre-flight, ask what is missing to act on it (screen, expected result) and write the answer on the task before coding it. When the task lists attachments (screenshots, documents copied into the project by Vibe Studio), read them first. A feedback given in the chat during this step is added the same way, as the next R task with "user feedback", before it is coded. Before coding a correction that changes the behaviour described in `plan.md`, ask the user and record the decision in `state/decisions.md`. Then redo the visual finish of the screens touched and run the end-to-end tests again; regenerated screenshots replace the old ones. Update a test only when the correction changes its walkthrough step. Show the corrected screens and ask the user to confirm each correction. Add a line to the phase 5 block of `state/journal.md` with the review ids corrected. Then suggest a new review round with `poc-6-review-scenario`, in a new Copilot session: it checks each correction.

11. Anchor check. Re-read the five hard constraints and confirm none was broken.

## Next step

Suggest the `poc-6-review-scenario` skill, in a new Copilot session (recommended), or as a new request in this session.
